title: Content & asset operations
subtitle: DAM, vocabulary, rights, lifecycle
summary: Keeping libraries searchable, terms agreed, usage visible, and published content on a review cycle.

story.label: Practice
story.title: The day-to-day of a library
story.body: This is the work that continues after a DAM or vocabulary is stood up: who owns a file, what it can be used for, when it comes back for review.

title: Content platforms & architecture
subtitle: CMS models, authoring, audits
summary: Reusable models, the forms editors type into, and the inventory that shows what to keep.

story.label: Practice
story.title: Fitting the platform to the task
story.body: If the model and the form don’t match how people publish, they work around both. These projects are about that fit: records, references and checks at the point of entry.

title: Editorial delivery & enablement
subtitle: Workflow, release, handover
summary: Getting work from request to live, then leaving the next owner able to run it without asking me.

story.label: Practice
story.title: From request to live, then handover
story.body: A workflow is only useful if it names an owner and a publish check. Handover is the same problem later: tasks, sources of truth, and who keeps the guidance current.
